title_vi: Các chính sách đẩy khóa ra khỏi bộ nhớ đệm

Tỷ lệ trúng là số đo để so các chính sách.

claims.claim_vi: Use allkeys-random when keys are accessed with roughly equal frequency, for example data read in a repeating cycle; Redis LRU is an approximation that samples keys; LFU is approximated with a probabilistic counter and a decay period so it adapts to changes in the access pattern.
claims.section: Eviction policies; Approximated LRU algorithm; LFU eviction
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of redis/docs at commit 3b030c7ef066c0bb7f88ddec02c784e49783b0f8, the head of its default branch when read on 2026-10-18 (a later change to that branch does not alter this URL).

claims.claim_vi: memcached's newer LRU splits into HOT, WARM and COLD; its primary goal is to better protect active items from scanning.
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of memcached/memcached at tag 1.6.24 (commit 1b3b8555734f9b7b8d979924c7f8d6cf82194ba8), the version that was run.

claims.claim_vi: Simulation, cache of 100 items, 100,000 accesses, hit ratios LRU/LFU/FIFO/random/MRU/SLRU: Zipf over 1,000 keys 57.9/65.5/52.4/52.3/12.6/65.5%; loop over 120 keys 0/0/0/68.5/83.1/0%; 70% to 50 hot keys and 30% one-off keys 64.4/70.0/52.3/52.6/1.3/70.0% (70% is the maximum).
claims.verified_by: Experiment run by the author on 2026-10-18 on one KVM virtual machine (4 vCPU): exact implementations in Python 3.13 (LFU ties broken by insertion order, SLRU with 80% protected, seeded random), Zipf distribution with exponent 1.

claims.claim_vi: Five eviction strategies: TTL, LRU, LFU, MRU (useful for scans and OS buffer caches), SLRU (probationary and protected segments).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

design_notes_vi: Một khung định nghĩa và ba khung kết quả, mỗi khung một kiểu truy cập, để thấy không chính sách nào thắng mọi nơi.
source_deviations: Source says the best strategy depends on context; the lesson shows that with a simulation and checks two of its conclusions against Redis and memcached documentation.
The simulation covers six policies (LRU, LFU, MRU, SLRU, plus FIFO and random for comparison); TTL is explained but not simulated, since it does not choose a key when the cache is full.
